About Tailscale 
 About the Role 
 Tailscale is looking for a pragmatic, business-minded Head of Legal to build and lead our legal function through our next stage of growth.
 As Tailscale’s senior legal leader, you’ll partner with executives and teams across the company to navigate complex legal and business considerations, manage risk, and build the capabilities needed to support a growing, globally distributed technology company.
 This is an opportunity to shape how Legal operates at Tailscale. You’ll establish priorities, advise on important company and product decisions, and determine the right combination of internal talent, outside counsel, processes, and systems to support the business. An early priority will be strengthening our commercial legal capabilities, including hiring a dedicated leader to own contracts and help scale our approach to commercial transactions.
 You may already lead a broad legal organization, or you may be an experienced legal leader who has taken on progressively greater responsibility and is ready to step into the top legal role for the first time. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Build and evolve the strategy, priorities, operating model, and team for Tailscale’s legal function.
 Serve as a trusted advisor to executives and cross-functional leaders, translating legal complexity into clear, practical business guidance.
 Help leaders identify material risks, evaluate tradeoffs, and move forward with appropriate safeguards.
 Partner with Product, Engineering, Security, Sales, Finance, People, Operations, Marketing, and other teams on company priorities.
 Advise across a range of matters that may include corporate governance, product development, open-source software, intellectual property, privacy, data, AI, security, employment, commercial relationships, compliance, and international operations.
 Build scalable legal processes, policies, systems, and decision-making frameworks without creating unnecessary complexity.
 Determine which legal capabilities should be developed internally, delegated to future team members, or supported by outside counsel.
 Hire and empower legal team members, including building a dedicated commercial legal capability.
 Select and manage outside counsel across the countries where Tailscale operates, balancing expertise, responsiveness, cost, and business impact.
 Coordinate guidance across jurisdictions and translate local requirements into practical, consistent company practices.
 Support strategic partnerships, corporate initiatives, and other business-critical matters as Tailscale continues to grow.
 Anticipate emerging legal and regulatory developments and help the company prepare for what comes next.
 What We Are Looking For 
 Significant legal experience, including meaningful in-house experience within a technology company and a track record of helping legal functions scale in startup or high-growth environments.
 A law degree and active membership in at least one applicable bar or equivalent authorization to practice law.
 Progressive growth in the scope, complexity, ownership, and influence of your work.
 Broad business judgment and the ability to navigate legal issues beyond a single area of specialization.
 Experience advising executives and senior leaders on complex or consequential decisions.
 The ability to understand business goals, identify material risks, and recommend practical paths forward.
 Experience partnering effectively with technical, operational, and commercial teams.
 Familiarity with the legal considerations facing a growing software or technology company.
 Experience working with outside counsel and turning specialized advice into clear recommendations for the business.
 A track record of building or improving legal capabilities, teams, programs, processes, or areas of practice.
 Strong communication skills and the ability to make complex issues understandable to different audiences.
 Sound judgment, curiosity, and the confidence to challenge constructively when needed.
 Comfort operating in ambiguity and moving between strategic leadership and hands-on execution.
 Admission and good standing with at least one applicable state, provincial, or other recognized bar association.
 Nice to Have 
 We do not expect candidates to bring experience in every area below. Relevant experience may include:
 Developer tools, infrastructure, cloud, networking, cybersecurity, data, or another technically complex software environment.
 Open-source software, licensing, developer ecosystems, APIs, integrations, marketplaces, or technology partnerships.
 Product counseling, privacy, data governance, cybersecurity, intellectual property, or emerging technology.
 AI-enabled products or the use of AI within company operations.
 Cloud, on-premises, self-hosted, or hybrid software offerings.
 Data residency, sovereignty, localization, or cross-border data considerations.
 Supporting employees or business operations across multiple countries.
 Corporate governance, financing, strategic transactions, or board-related matters.
 Building or scaling a legal function within a growth-stage company.
 Hiring, developing, or leading in-house legal professionals.
 How You’ll Work 
 At Tailscale, Legal is a thoughtful and pragmatic partner. You’ll seek to understand the goals behind the work, help teams evaluate tradeoffs, and build frameworks that enable people to make sound decisions with increasing independence.
 You’ll thrive in this role if you enjoy building, are curious about technical products, and want to shape a legal function as the company grows. You know when to engage directly, when to bring in specialized expertise, and when to empower others to lead.
 As a company, we strive to maintain fair and equitable compensation practices within our team across all roles and all levels. Tailscale's compensation package includes base salary, equity, and comprehensive benefits. The salary range displayed on each job posting represents the target range for a new hire's base salary. Individual offers may vary based on experience and skill set.
 CAN Pay Range
 $298,820 — $427,460 CAD 
 What We Offer 
 A competitive total compensation package. This includes a base salary, an equity incentive plan and variable commission (for quota-based roles).
 Support for your personal and professional development. Grow your career thoughtfully with $1500 USD annually for professional development, or take advantage of mentorship, coaching, and internal promotion opportunities. 
 A build-your-own home office setup. You choose your own company-owned laptop (Mac or PC), receive a monthly home internet reimbursement, and $500 USD to customize your workstation to make it your own.

As the Safety and Systems Technical Program Manager, you will drive the execution of our safety and systems engineering development efforts for our autonomous vehicle platforms. Safety is at the core of everything we do, and we need a technical program manager to ensure our safety assessments, system architectures, and verification and validation processes (simulation and real world testing) are delivered efficiently and rigorously. You will translate complex technical milestones into clear, centralized plans, streamline communication across engineering leads, and leverage modern AI tools to eliminate administrative friction. If you thrive on bringing structure to safety-critical engineering, aligning cross-functional teams, and clearing roadblocks before they happen, this role is for you.
 
You will:
Collaborate with other Technical Program Managers across the company to ensure Safety, Security, and Systems plans align seamlessly with other functional areas and the organization’s feature introduction roadmap.
Consolidate project timelines, Jira tracking boards, and status updates into a centralized master plan, utilizing AI tools (like Claude) to synthesize information and limit the manual overhead required from engineering leads.
Provide clear, comprehensive executive reporting of Safety, Security, and Systems tasks, deliverables, and resources across multiple assessments, platforms, and behavioral competencies.
Track the execution of verification and validation (V&V) in simulation and real-world testing - providing dedicated TPM support to test leads so they can focus on test definition and evaluation - while applying systems engineering principles to ensure all requirements have full test coverage.
Take a leading role in organizing driverless deployment decisions through Production Readiness Reviews (PRR), coordinating the delivery of safety and Security artifacts to ensure they meet internal quality gates and timeline expectations.
Lead the alignment of continuous software evaluation activities, ensuring the Safety, Security, and Systems teams provide the right deliverables adapted to various product maturity and deployment phases.
Establish efficient issue burndown tracking methods, acting as the central liaison to route identified process, anomaly, and system performance issues to the appropriate stakeholders and drive them to resolution.

Qualifications:
5+ years of technical program management experience, with a track record of leading complex, cross-functional technical programs.
Direct experience in autonomous vehicles, robotics, aerospace, or another safety-critical environment spanning hardware, software, and systems.
Strong technical fluency in systems engineering, safety assurance and requirements management.
Hands-on experience with program tracking tools such as Jira, and a strong inclination to use modern AI solutions to streamline operational tracking and speed up critical decisions.
Excellent written and verbal communication; comfortable summarizing complex technical statuses for leadership and facilitating working-level reviews.
BS or MS in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field.

Bonus/nice to have:
Deep understanding of the autonomous trucking domain and commercial rollouts.
Proven history of establishing single-source-of-truth planning systems across highly distributed teams.
Experience executing production readiness reviews (PRR).

Résumé du Rôle 
 SMARDT poursuit l’expansion de ses activités en Amérique du Nord et est à la recherche d’ un(e)   
 responsable de la qualité des fournisseurs (SQL) qui sera chargé de s'assurer que les fournisseurs livrent des matériaux, des produits et des services conformes aux exigences établies en matière d'ingénierie, de qualité, de réglementation et de clients. Le SQL est chargé d'assister la chaîne d'approvisionnement dans la sélection et l'évaluation des nouveaux fournisseurs et de surveiller leurs performances sur la base des procédures et normes SMARDT établies. Ce poste implique une collaboration étroite avec les services Achats, Chaîne d'approvisionnement, Ingénierie, Fabrication et les principaux fournisseurs afin de favoriser l'amélioration continue, d'améliorer la ponctualité des livraisons et la qualité, de résoudre efficacement les problèmes, défaillances et défauts signalés, et de réduire/atténuer les risques conformément à l'engagement de SMARDT envers ses clients.
 Le SQL joue un rôle essentiel dans la protection de l'intégrité des produits, la réduction des coûts liés à la mauvaise qualité (COPQ) chez les fournisseurs et le renforcement des performances de ces derniers.
 Il s'agit d'un poste à   100 % sur site   et vous travaillerez au quotidien aux côtés de notre équipe.
 Principales Responsabilités 
 Gestion de la qualité des fournisseurs 
 Élaborer et mettre en œuvre une stratégie de qualité des fournisseurs alignée sur les objectifs stratégiques de l'entreprise.
 Diriger les processus de qualification, d'intégration et d'approbation des fournisseurs.
 Être capable d'améliorer la qualité et la capacité de production des fournisseurs
 Réaliser des évaluations des risques et des performances des fournisseurs.
 Définir et surveiller les indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) des fournisseurs (taux de défauts/PPM, respect des délais de livraison, réactivité face aux mesures correctives, etc.).
 Veiller au respect de la norme ISO 9001 et des exigences internes en matière de qualité.
 Établir et mettre en œuvre les exigences de qualité des fournisseurs (inspection, essais, documentation, emballage, processus spéciaux)
 Les voyages d'affaires sont fort probables avec des visites aux états-unis et a travers le Canada.
 Veiller à la mise en œuvre des exigences FAI / PPAP le cas échéant  Audits et développement des fournisseurs 
 Planifier et mener des évaluations et des audits de fournisseurs sur site et/ou à distance.
 Diriger les processus d'actions correctives fournisseurs (SCAR) à l'aide de rapports de contrôle des non-conformités et d'analyses des causes profondes telles que la méthode 8D, le diagramme en arête de poisson ou des méthodologies équivalentes.
 Collaborer avec les fournisseurs pour mettre en œuvre des actions correctives et préventives durables.
 Mener des initiatives d'amélioration continue avec les fournisseurs stratégiques.
 Gestion des non-conformités et des escalades 
 Diriger les enquêtes sur les causes profondes liées aux défauts des fournisseurs.
 Coordonner la maîtrise, le traitement et la résolution des problèmes liés aux fournisseurs.
 Gérer les refacturations aux fournisseurs et le recouvrement des coûts liés aux non-conformités, le cas échéant.
 Signaler les risques critiques liés aux fournisseurs à la direction et soutenir les stratégies d'atténuation.
 Servir de point de contact principal pour les questions de qualité des fournisseurs au sein des équipes interfonctionnelles
 Définir les exigences de qualité des fournisseurs pour les aspects de fabrication, d'inspection et de test, ainsi que pour l'emballage et l'expédition, y compris les certificats, registres et documents de test à fournir dans le cadre de la livraison,
 Collaborer avec le service des achats pour la sélection des fournisseurs et l'évaluation de leurs performances.
 Assister les sites de fabrication pour les questions de qualité liées aux fournisseurs.
 Tenir à jour les tableaux de bord de qualité des fournisseurs et les rapports destinés à la direction.
 Analyser les tendances de performance afin d'atténuer de manière proactive les risques liés à la chaîne d'approvisionnement.
 Profil Recherché 
 Compétences : 
 Plus de 5 ans d'expérience dans le domaine de la qualité des fournisseurs, de la fabrication ou du développement des fournisseurs.
 Expérience dans un environnement de fabrication réglementé ou de haute précision.
 Expérience avérée dans la conduite d'audits fournisseurs et la mise en œuvre de mesures correctives.
 Solide connaissance des systèmes qualité.
 Analyse des causes profondes (5-Pourquoi, diagramme en arête de poisson, 8D)
 PPAP, APQP, FMEA SPC et outils d'analyse de données
 Systèmes ERP/MRP
 Bon jugement et connaissance du calcul des coûts liés aux défauts des fournisseurs
 Connaissance pratique des normes ISO
 Compte tenu de la nature des tâches liées à ce poste, notamment des échanges avec l'étranger, la maîtrise de l'anglais est un atout indispensable pour occuper ce poste.
 Profil Académique et Expérience

Position description 
 The McGill University Department of Neurology and Neurosurgery in the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences invites applications for a full-time Contract Academic Staff position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor (Clinical) specializing in Adult Epilepsy. We welcome applications from outstanding clinical epileptologists (MD) and clinician-scientists (MD/PhD). The professorial rank will be determined according to the successful candidate’s qualifications and experience. This will be a three-year, Contract Academic Staff position and does not confer eligibility for tenure. 
 The successful candidate will join the McGill University Department of Neurology and Neurosurgery and be based at the Montreal Neurological Institute and Hospital (The Neuro)—a major teaching hospital affiliated with the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences at Canada’s internationally known McGill University, located in the vibrant and multicultural city of Montreal, in the province of Quebec. The Neuro is an internationally recognized centre for excellence in clinical care, research, and education in epilepsy. The Neuro's Epilepsy Program brings together internationally renowned clinicians, clinician-scientists, and basic scientists in a highly collaborative environment dedicated to improving the understanding and treatment of epilepsy. The program provides comprehensive tertiary and quaternary epilepsy care, evaluating approximately 200 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy annually through its Epilepsy Monitoring Unit for presurgical assessment, while the outpatient epilepsy clinics provide care for more than 4,500 patients each year. 
 The close integration of clinical care, research, and education provides an exceptional environment for innovation, translational research, and advanced subspecialty training. The Epilepsy Program collaborates extensively across McGill University and its affiliated research institutes, including the Neuro's McConnell Brain Imaging Centre, which houses state-of-the-art neuroimaging facilities, including 3T and 7T MRI, MEG, and PET. The program also features advanced high-density EEG, MRI-compatible EEG, and neuromodulation technologies, providing a unique platform for both clinical and research innovation. 
 Across its universities and research institutes, Montreal is a leader in artificial intelligence research, further adding to the vibrant environment supporting top-notch neuroscience. The Neuro is an Open Science institution. Graduate training is offered through the Integrated Program in Neuroscience, an inter-Faculty program that is the largest of its kind in Canada. 
 McGill University was founded in 1819 and is consistently ranked among the top 30 public universities in the world and among the top three in Canada, while its medical school is consistently ranked first in Canada. McGill’s official language is English, and it is located in Montreal ( http://www.montrealinternational.com/en/ ), a multicultural, multilingual city with a sparkling cultural life.  Contribute to the education and mentorship of patients, medical students, residents, fellows, graduate trainees, and allied health professionals. 
 Advance the academic mission of the Department through leadership, scholarship, interdisciplinary collaboration, knowledge translation, and contributions to institutional, provincial, national, and international epilepsy initiatives.

Hi 👋🏾, I’m Abhik https://www.linkedin.com/in/abhikpramanik/, Ashby’s Co-Founder and CTO. We’re looking for a great (former) engineer who built impressive products and now builds teams of great engineers. Ashby’s success and ambition mean we’re doubling the Engineering team in the next year, and we need your experience and leadership to do it thoughtfully.

Our product and growth are exceptional. Ashby All-in-One is powerful, easy to use, and replaces several venture-backed companies' worth of products (often with a better experience). We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway.

A big part of our secret sauce is how we run Engineering. We achieve incredible speed and quality by discarding many industry norms and being optimistic about Engineers. We consider what makes exceptional Engineers exceptional, figure out how to hire them, and build an environment that gives them the freedom and agency to actually be exceptional. In other words, if engineers writing product specs, making product decisions, and not breaking down projects into individual tickets excites you, you’ve found the right place.

As an Engineering Manager, you’ll work closely with me, Ben, Colin, and your peers to build out the team and continue scaling this unique culture.

You’ll first do that through grassroots leadership. You’ll manage three to five Engineers and hire three to five more. They’ll cover multiple teams and a variety of specializations, from Product Engineers to Site Reliability Engineers to Design Engineers. Your day-to-day will include:

 - Providing feedback on product and technical specs to help engineers identify where to cut scope or improve quality. You don’t make the final decisions, but you’ll influence and coach ICs to reach the right ones.

 - Grow engineers to the point where they can take large, loosely defined projects and deliver them with little intervention.

 - Jump into our systems and code to debug a customer issue, ship a small bug fix, or improve our developer experience. Engineering leaders at Ashby are great engineers and enjoy keeping their skills up-to-date (while staying off the critical path).

You’ll also propose and lead department and company-wide initiatives. Some examples:

 - Rethink how we (and the industry) do pull request reviews by aligning on goals with the team, sampling a set of PRs to understand how effective they are, and writing a proposal to the team about what we could change to speed up reviews while giving reviewers the time and space to give useful feedback.

 - Design and improve interviews based on candidate and team feedback. We pride ourselves on thoughtful interviews that simulate actually working with us!

 - Improve how we generate and simulate data in demo accounts. It’s a project off the critical path, but it helps you keep up-to-date on our codebase while immensely impacting the business, from Engineering to QA to Sales.

I’ll share more details once we meet.

 

WHAT WE’RE BUILDING

As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition (TA) software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help.

As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!

As we’ve set the standard for excellence in TA software, HR teams have pulled us into solving their problems in areas like onboarding and performance management.

 

WHY YOU SHOULDN’T APPLY

 - You don’t enjoy coding or don’t find time to stay up-to-date on technology. We believe great leaders are folks who were great engineers themselves. That starts with loving the craft and never giving it up.

 - You follow the rules and accept the hand you’ve been dealt. We want folks with the ambition, courage, and follow-through to change things, whether it’s within their own team or across departments.

 - You went into management because it was the only growth path available. We want folks who could have been Principal engineers (or were one!).

 - You're happy with a team of engineers who are predominantly early-career or mid-career or don't thrive with ownership or autonomy. You believe that with enough guardrails, the team can get things done.

 - To you, a Staff or Principal Engineer is someone who spends most of their time project managing or conducting architecture reviews. You don’t believe staff and principal engineers could lead by the example they set or the leverage they create through their work.

 - You’re not optimistic or convinced that we can build a large engineering team that functions differently from the status quo. You think, at some size, common processes need to be implemented to ensure consistent product delivery (e.g., sprint planning, product managers writing in-depth specifications). You might not say it out loud, but you think, at some size, compromises have to be made for the sake of hiring numbers or consistency.

 

ENGINEERING CULTURE

Our engineering culture is motivated by Benji’s (my Co-founder and CEO) and my belief that a small, talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!). We do it through:

 - Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design

 - Natural collaboration and deliberate communication

 - Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage

 - Putting effort into building a diverse team

 

MINIMAL PROCESS & LOTS OF OWNERSHIP

The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They took customer problems and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise.

Traditional product-development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But, consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”

At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, at Ashby, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive.

 

COLLABORATION IS NATURAL & COMMUNICATION IS DELIBERATE

Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here https://www.ashbyhq.com/team!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in <2h meetings per week (I wrote about it here https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/company/thoughtful-communication).

To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over 4 years. ~34 hours of focus time, 2.5h of interviews, and 3.5 hours of meetings:

 
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/4ea5f68e-c33e-4ac9-831a-e732bee4a303/d4679311-9dba-4031-bf5e-19ce78597ab1/calendar.png]
 

We also meet in person at least twice a year, once as a department and once as a company. You also have a small budget to meet up with folks in your city/region.

 

INCREASE LEVERAGE, NOT TEAM SIZE

We built Ashby with the quality, breadth, and depth that many customers would expect from much larger teams over larger time scales. We’ve done this through investment in:

 - Great developer tooling. Our CI/CD takes ~10m, and we deploy at least 15x a day. A debugger that works out of the box. Everyone on the team has contributed to our developer experience 💪🏾.

 - Building blocks to create powerful and customizable products fast. At the core of Ashby is a set of common components (analytics modeling and query language, policy engine, workflow engine, design system) that we constantly improve. Each improvement to a common component cascades throughout our app (short video below).

 - AI-powered tooling. We think of AI as a way to automate the mundane parts of building and maintaining high-quality software. We use a combination of third-party and internally built tools that, for instance, auto-triage customer issues, suggest fixes, prototype ideas, generate production-ready code, and conduct code reviews. Engineers have an unlimited token budget (but are not measured on it). We write in detail about our philosophy, current use of AI, and future plans for AI in Engineering here https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/engineering/ai-ashby-engineering-and-the-future.

Here’s an impromptu quote from Arjun in our company Slack of what it’s like to build a feature at Ashby:

 
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/4ea5f68e-c33e-4ac9-831a-e732bee4a303/8d94727a-46d8-42a2-9627-ddcd7f822f95/arjun.png]
 

And a demo of one of these building blocks:

PUT EFFORT INTO DIVERSITY

Diverse teams drive innovation and better outcomes. Having seen my mother and partner build their careers as minority women in non-diverse fields, I want to make sure Ashby creates opportunities for the next generation of engineers from underrepresented groups.

Today, 25% of engineers and 50% of our engineering leaders at Ashby are from underrepresented groups. We are taking conscious steps to improve, like sourcing diverse candidates, providing generous paid family leave, no leetcode interviews, and more.

 

WORK-LIFE BALANCE: IT’S A MARATHON, NOT A SPRINT

The intensity of work at Ashby should feel like a marathon, not a sprint (nor speed-walking). We work with urgency and ambition to build excellent software, but we don’t need to prove out a new software category or product-market fit. That requires ingenuity and thoughtfulness, and that doesn’t happen with unrealistic deadlines or sleepless nights.

Our remote, low-meeting, high-ownership culture gives you a lot of flexibility in how you structure your days and weeks. In practice, that means you keep your own hours, but there will be moments of intensity, like launching your feature at our annual user conference. We offer unlimited PTO, and you actually get to use it. Some of our most exceptional engineers take almost 30 days of vacation per year.

This way of working allows many of us on the team to be active parents, including Benji and me. I block off 1.5 hours every morning to spend with my daughter and drop her off at school.  Mujda https://www.linkedin.com/in/mujdaalamzai/ (Product Engineer) puts it best in an article https://nextplayso.substack.com/p/should-you-join-ashby about us: “I can say that Ashby is a great place to be a mom… No one bats an eye if I have to take my kid to a doctor’s appointment or have to work weird hours because childcare fell through.”

 

INTERVIEW PROCESS

This is an important role and our interview process reflects that both in challenge and length (5h 15m):

 1. Introduction call with Ben (30m, live)

 2. A technical screen where you and Ben pair in our actual codebase (1h, live)

 3. An interview with Ben to explore your past experience as a leader (1h, live)

 4. Interview with Abhik, VP of Engineering (45m, live)

 5. Interview with Colin, Head of Engineering EMEA (30m, live)

 6. Final round where you meet Engineers and other Engineering Managers (90m, live)

Depending on my bandwidth, we may start with an additional 30m screen with a recruiter. Near the end of the process, we’ll do reference checks.

This is also an important decision for you, so I’m always happy to have coffee chats in person or over Zoom to get to know each other. If we don’t move forward, we’re happy to share feedback.

 

YOUR FIRST SIX MONTHS AT ASHBY

Portless is changing the face of global e-commerce. By decoupling brands from traditional, expensive domestic warehousing, we allow e-commerce companies to ship directly from manufacturing hubs to global consumers in as little as 3-5 days. We are growing fast, and we are looking for an elite, full-stack engineer to help us scale a world-class, globally distributed platform to power the future of cross-border logistics.
 The Role
 We are looking for a high-leverage, senior full-stack operator to own and scale major pillars of our global supply chain orchestration platform. In this role, you aren’t just taking tickets and writing code; you will own entire architectural modules from end-to-end.
 You will build out our B2B merchant portal, optimize our core logistics engine, and design heavy-duty API integrations connecting Portless to major Order, Warehouse, and Transportation Management Systems (OMS/WMS/TMS). This is a role for a highly autonomous, deeply curious engineer who thrives in an asynchronous, remote environment and loves solving the messy, complex problems that happen when software meets the physical world.
 The Tech Stack
 We build on a modern, fully serverless, cloud-native, and event-driven architecture.
 Backend & Infrastructure: Node.js, Express, TypeScript, Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
 Databases & Analytics: Cloud SQL / PostgreSQL, Firestore, ClickHouse, BigQuery.
 Frontend: React, Vite.js, TypeScript.
 What You’ll Do
 Own the Solution: Take broad, high-level product requirements and turn them into production-ready features. You will be responsible for the full lifecycle of your code—from schema design to slick, intuitive frontend experiences.
 Build Resilient Core Infrastructure: Architect and develop critical modules that coordinate international shipping routes, customs data, and real-time package tracking. Because global supply chains never sleep, you will design these workflows to be highly fault-tolerant and resilient to external network errors.
 Deep Integration Work: Build and maintain heavy-duty API integrations with enterprise OMS, WMS, and TMS platforms. You will implement robust retry strategies, idempotency keys, and dead-letter queues to handle the chaotic nature of physical-world data synchronization.
 Drive Asynchronous Momentum: Work seamlessly across a globally distributed team (USA, Canada, EU, UK, China). You write clear documentation, communicate proactively in public channels, and don't need real-time meetings to make meaningful progress.
 Maintain High Engineering Standards: Participate in rigorous asynchronous code reviews. Help us maintain elite DORA metrics by ensuring your code is modular, heavily tested, and highly observable so we can keep our Change Failure Rate low.
 What We’re Looking For
 The Self-Driving Engineer: 5+ years of professional full-stack experience (TypeScript / Node.js / React), ideally in a fast-paced, high-growth startup environment. You are entirely comfortable with ambiguity, know how to unblock yourself, take extreme pride in ownership, and demonstrate a clear mindset for owning the solution from conception to deployment.
 AI Fluency: You are a power user of modern AI development tools (e.g., Cursor, Copilot, Claude Code) and treat them as an extension of your own capability. You leverage AI throughout the entire lifecycle—not just for coding, but for discovery, architectural setup, and complex solution design. You bring a 'product owner' mindset to your AI usage: you are detail-oriented, maintain a big-picture view, and know how to direct AI to solve business-critical problems, while always maintaining a sharp human eye to catch hallucinations or architectural drift.
 Distributed Systems Mindset: Proven track record building cloud-native, event-driven architectures. You have deep experience designing fault-tolerant systems and know how to handle race conditions, eventual consistency, split-brain scenarios, and flaky third-party APIs.
 Data & Storage Pragmatism: You understand when to use a relational database (PostgreSQL), when to leverage NoSQL/document stores (Firestore), and how to work alongside real-time analytical engines (ClickHouse) or deep data warehouses (BigQuery).
 Deep Curiosity & Attention to Detail: You don't just paste together answers or accept "it works" on the surface. You go deep into the stack to understand why something breaks, obsess over edge cases, and think about how your code behaves at scale.
 Distributed Native & Team Player: Proven experience working effectively in a globally distributed, asynchronous environment. You excel at written communication, keep projects moving across time zones, and naturally serve as a collaborative team player. You proactively assist others without being prompted, identifying opportunities to support the team’s success, and always prioritize shared wins over individual recognition.
 Bonus Points (Nice-to-Haves)
 Deep experience with the GCP / Firebase ecosystem (especially Firestore and Data Connect at scale).
 Direct experience building systems in Logistics, Supply Chain, FinTech, or E-commerce verticals.
 Previous experience integrating with enterprise e-commerce platforms (Shopify, WooCommerce) or global shipping/carrier APIs.
 Why Portless?
 Competitive salary + meaningful equity package.
 Flexible, remote-first, and asynchronous-friendly work environment across multiple time zones.
 The chance to solve massive, tangible global trade problems alongside a highly focused, elite engineering team.

You will work closely with cross-functional teams, including researchers, engineers, and data annotators, to conduct data-driven decision-making and improve the overall effectiveness of our AI systems.

This role combines expertise in statistics, experimental design incl. human annotators, and machine learning to ensure that our models are trained on high-quality data and perform reliably across diverse scenarios. You will contribute to Cohere’s mission of advancing AI by ensuring our systems are robust, scalable, and impactful.

 - Analyse and assess the generalisability and robustness of ML systems across diverse use cases.

 - Collaborate with teams to improve dataset quality and model performance.

 - Train and fine-tune large language models (LLMs) on distributed training infrastructures.
